chapter: Package shows, Miami and the USO
title: USO tour continued: Germany, Korea and Japan
summary: After France and Germany, Korea with Budd Johnson, Pruitt and Peacock.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Oh she had her own arrangements?
Yeah.
For a small band?
We had eight pieces.
When did this USO thing break up? You spent all of August in France.
We spent all of August in France, in Germany September--part of September anyway and then we came back and played New York for a couple of weeks and I did a few gigs that
With this band?
Yeah; I kept everybody together.
You were keeping them together?
Oh, yeah.
These were not steady, these were not long terms jobs, were they?
I had contracts for the whole year.
But that's USO.
USO.
I'm not talking about-- there were no night clubs?
No, I didn't like it. I liked to tour.
We stayed in New York a few weeks and then we went to Korea.
Korea is in '53 mostly, late '52?
That was the end of that thing, wasn't it?
We went to Japan after.
Bud Johnson's on this, isn't he?
Bud Johnson was on the European tour. I took Bernie Peacock.
That's where you got Bernie Peacock and Pruitt; two headaches. It's a wonder they didn't get shot by the enemy over there.

That's when they made me an honorary member of the Second Division. We played at a couple of the EVAC hospitals, right behind the lines, where they would pick them up in the helicopter and bring them back there.
How was Budd on the tour? Budd was all right, wasn't he?
Fine.
He could arrange like
mad too.
He made some arrangements for me too. He made some beautiful arrangements.
When you came back from Korea, that was it, isn't it, for the USO, for the time being?
Yeah, that was it for a while.
When you came out of the USO, that was the last USO trip you made for quite a while, in '53, wasn't it?
Right.
